definition: To enter a building by force to steal.
examples: Someone broke into our car.
Thieves broke into the store last night.
He was caught breaking into a house.

spanish.definition: Entrar a un edificio a la fuerza para robar.

definition: To return something; to make you remember.
examples: Please bring back my book tomorrow.
This song brings back memories.
She brought back gifts from Peru.

definition: To make something lower; to make a government lose power.
examples: This medicine will bring down your fever.
They want to bring down prices.
The scandal brought down the government.

spanish.definition: Hacer que algo baje; hacer caer un gobierno.

definition: To earn money; to ask someone to help.
examples: The store brings in $5,000 a week.
They brought in an expert.
Bring in the chairs from outside.

spanish.definition: Ganar dinero; pedirle ayuda a alguien.

definition: To phone your work or a radio show.
examples: He called in sick today.
Listeners can call in with questions.
She called in to say she was late.

spanish.definition: Llamar al trabajo o a un programa de radio.

definition: To become popular; to start to understand.
examples: The new game caught on fast.
He finally caught on to the joke.
Will this style catch on?

definition: To make sure someone or something is OK.
examples: The nurse checked up on the patient.
My mom always checks up on me.
I'm just checking up on you.

spanish.definition: Asegurarse de que alguien o algo está bien.

definition: To stop a business for good.
examples: The factory closed down last year.
Many stores are closing down.
They closed down the old cinema.

definition: To move lower; to become less.
examples: Come down from the tree!
Prices have come down.
The rain came down all night.

definition: To trust someone to help you.
examples: You can count on me.
I'm counting on you to be there.
She always counted on her father.

spanish.definition: Confiar en que alguien te ayude.

definition: To take action to solve a problem.
examples: I'll deal with it tomorrow.
She deals with angry customers every day.
He dealt with the problem quickly.

definition: To wear nice clothes or a costume.
examples: We dressed up for the party.
The kids dressed up as pirates.
You don't need to dress up.

spanish.definition: Ponerse ropa elegante o un disfraz.

definition: To visit without planning.
examples: Drop in anytime.
My aunt dropped in yesterday.
She's dropping in on her way home.

definition: To not do as much as you should.
examples: He fell behind in math.
Don't fall behind with your rent.
We're falling behind schedule.

definition: To fall in love with someone; to be tricked by something.
examples: She fell for him right away.
Don't fall for that old trick.
I almost fell for his lies.

definition: To throw away or remove something.
examples: We need to get rid of these old clothes.
I can't get rid of this cold.
She got rid of her old car.

definition: To give something to many people; to stop working.
examples: They gave out free samples.
The teacher is giving out the tests.
My legs gave out after the race.

spanish.definition: Dar algo a mucha gente; dejar de funcionar.

definition: To become lower; to stop working.
examples: Prices went down last month.
The sun goes down at six.
The website went down for an hour.

spanish.definition: Volverse más bajo; dejar de funcionar.

definition: To choose; to try to get something.
examples: I'll go for the chicken.
Go for it!
She's going for the gold medal.

definition: To become higher.
examples: Rent went up again.
Prices are going up.
The temperature will go up tomorrow.

definition: To look good together; to choose.
examples: This tie goes with your suit.
Red wine goes with meat.
I'll go with the blue one.

definition: To give something to each person in a group.
examples: The teacher handed out the tests.
They're handing out free coffee.
She handed out flyers on the street.

spanish.definition: Dar algo a cada persona de un grupo.

definition: To stay in a place doing nothing special.
examples: The kids hang around the mall.
Don't hang around here.
He hung around after the party.

spanish.definition: Estar en un lugar sin hacer nada especial.

definition: To leave.
examples: We should head out soon.
They headed out early in the morning.
I'm heading out now; see you later.

definition: To get news from someone.
examples: Have you heard from your brother?
I hope to hear from you soon.
We haven't heard from her in months.

definition: To help someone, especially for a short time.
examples: Can you help out on Saturday?
My neighbor helped out with the kids.
She's helping out at the school.

spanish.definition: Ayudar a alguien, sobre todo por un tiempo corto.

definition: To stop yourself from doing something; to keep someone from moving forward.
examples: She held back her tears.
Fear is holding back your success.
Don't hold back; tell me everything.

spanish.definition: Evitar hacer algo; impedir que alguien avance.

definition: To make someone late; to rob with a gun.
examples: Sorry, I got held up in traffic.
Two men held up the bank.
What's holding up the line?

spanish.definition: Hacer llegar tarde a alguien; robar con un arma.

definition: To take part in an activity.
examples: Everyone joined in the singing.
Can I join in?
The kids are joining in the game.

definition: To stay at a distance.
examples: Keep away from the fire.
Kids must keep away from the pool.
She kept away from him all night.

definition: To not enter; to stop someone from entering.
examples: The sign says keep out.
A fence keeps out the deer.
Keep out of my room!

definition: To force someone to leave.
examples: They kicked out the drunk man.
She was kicked out of school.
The landlord is kicking out the tenants.

definition: To destroy a building; to hit someone so they fall.
examples: They knocked down the old house.
A car knocked down a man.
They're knocking down the wall.

spanish.definition: Destruir un edificio; golpear a alguien hasta tumbarlo.

definition: To hit something so it falls.
examples: The cat knocked over my glass.
He knocked over a lamp.
Don't knock over the vase.

spanish.definition: Golpear algo para que se caiga.

definition: To allow someone to enter.
examples: Please let in the dog.
They didn't let us in.
Open the window to let in some air.

definition: To allow someone to leave; to make a sound.
examples: Let out the cat, please.
She let out a scream.
School lets out at three.

spanish.definition: Permitir que alguien salga; hacer un sonido.

definition: To stand in a line.
examples: People lined up for tickets.
Line up at the door, kids.
Fans are lining up outside.

definition: To have money or food to stay alive.
examples: They live on $2,000 a month.
He lived on rice and beans.
You can't live on chocolate.

spanish.definition: Tener dinero o comida para sobrevivir.

definition: To lock all the doors; to put someone in prison.
examples: Lock up before you leave.
They locked up the thief.
He's locking up the store.

spanish.definition: Cerrar todas las puertas; meter a alguien en la cárcel.

definition: To visit and see a place.
examples: We looked around the old town.
Can I look around the house?
She's looking around the store.

definition: To think about the past.
examples: Looking back, I made a mistake.
He never looks back.
She looked back on her childhood.

definition: To think you are better than someone.
examples: She looks down on poor people.
Don't look down on others.
He looked down on his coworkers.

spanish.definition: Creer que eres mejor que alguien.

definition: To try to find out about something.
examples: The police are looking into the crime.
I'll look into it.
We looked into buying a house.

definition: To be similar in appearance; to seem likely.
examples: She looks like her mother.
It looks like rain.
What does he look like?

definition: To check something quickly.
examples: Can you look over my essay?
She looked over the contract.
He's looking over the menu.

definition: To see or hear something with difficulty.
examples: I can't make out the words.
She could just make out a face in the dark.
Can you make out that sign?

spanish.definition: Ver u oír algo con dificultad.

definition: To not have a chance to do something good.
examples: Don't miss out on this sale.
I missed out on the party.
You're missing out!

spanish.definition: No tener la oportunidad de hacer algo bueno.

definition: To confuse two things.
examples: I always mix up their names.
Don't mix up the files.
She mixed up the dates.

definition: To start something new; to stop thinking about the past.
examples: It's time to move on.
She moved on after the divorce.
Let's move on to the next question.

spanish.definition: Empezar algo nuevo; dejar de pensar en el pasado.

definition: To talk about your feelings; to open.
examples: He finally opened up about his problems.
A new store opened up downtown.
Open up! It's the police.

definition: To pay all of a debt; to bring a good result.
examples: We paid off the house.
All that hard work paid off.
She's paying off her credit card.

spanish.definition: Pagar toda una deuda; dar un buen resultado.

definition: To treat someone badly again and again.
examples: The older boys picked on him.
Stop picking on your sister.
She was picked on at school.

spanish.definition: Tratar mal a alguien una y otra vez.

definition: To connect a machine to electricity.
examples: Plug in the TV.
I plugged in my phone.
Is the printer plugged in?

spanish.definition: Conectar una máquina a la electricidad.

definition: To return something to its place.
examples: Put back the milk when you're done.
She put back the book on the shelf.
He's putting back the chairs.

spanish.definition: Poner algo otra vez en su lugar.

definition: To place something on a surface; to say bad things about someone.
examples: Put down that knife!
He always puts down his wife.
She put down her bags and sat.

spanish.definition: Poner algo en una superficie; hablar mal de alguien.

definition: To build something from parts.
examples: He put together the new desk.
We put together a team.
She's putting together a plan.

spanish.definition: Construir algo a partir de piezas.

definition: To charge someone too much money.
examples: Some taxi drivers rip off tourists.
That store ripped off a lot of customers.
Tourists often get ripped off.

definition: To hit someone with a car; to go past the time.
examples: A car ran over our cat.
The meeting ran over by an hour.
Be careful; don't run over the kids' bikes.

spanish.definition: Golpear a alguien con un carro; pasarse de la hora.

definition: To keep money for something special.
examples: I'm saving up for a car.
She saved up for a trip to Europe.
We saved up for years.

definition: To sell all of something.
examples: The tickets sold out in an hour.
They sold out of bread.
The concert is selling out fast.

spanish.definition: Vender todo lo que hay de algo.

definition: To return something by mail.
examples: I sent back the shoes because they were too small.
He sent back the soup.
We're sending back the broken TV.

definition: To become calm; to start living a quiet life.
examples: Settle down, kids!
He wants to settle down and have a family.
The baby finally settled down.

spanish.definition: Calmarse; empezar a vivir una vida tranquila.

definition: To compare prices in different stores.
examples: Shop around before you buy a car.
We shopped around for the best price.
I'm shopping around for a new phone.

definition: To guide someone through a place.
examples: She showed around the new teachers.
Can you show around the new students?
Who's going to show around the visitors?

spanish.definition: Guiar a alguien por un lugar.

definition: To sit with a straight back.
examples: Sit up straight!
She sat up in bed.
The patient is sitting up now.

definition: To stay the night at someone's house.
examples: Can my friend sleep over tonight?
She slept over at her cousin's house.
The kids are sleeping over at Grandma's.

spanish.definition: Pasar la noche en casa de alguien.

definition: To go faster.
examples: The car sped up.
Can you speed up the process?
We need to speed up.

definition: To end a relationship; to separate into groups.
examples: They split up after five years.
Let's split up and look for the dog.
Her parents are splitting up.

spanish.definition: Terminar una relación; dividirse en grupos.

definition: To be a short form of something; to support an idea.
examples: What does USA stand for?
I won't stand for this.
The party stands for freedom.

spanish.definition: Ser la forma corta de algo; apoyar una idea.

definition: To begin again.
examples: Let's start over.
She started over in a new city.
I made a mistake, so I'm starting over.

definition: To stay at home.
examples: Let's stay in tonight.
We stayed in because of the rain.
I'm staying in and watching a movie.

definition: To not come home; to not get involved.
examples: Don't stay out too late.
She stayed out all night.
Stay out of my business!

spanish.definition: No volver a casa; no involucrarse.

definition: To become involved to help.
examples: The teacher stepped in to stop the fight.
The government had to step in.
She's stepping in for the sick manager.

definition: To be easy to notice; to come out of something.
examples: His ears stick out.
She really sticks out in a crowd.
A nail is sticking out of the wall.

spanish.definition: Ser fácil de notar; salir de algo.

definition: To turn off a machine.
examples: Switch off the lights, please.
He switched off the TV.
She's switching off her phone.

definition: To turn on a machine.
examples: Switch on the light.
He switched on the radio.
She's switching on her laptop.

definition: To look after someone or something.
examples: She takes care of her little brother.
Who will take care of the dog?
I'll take care of the bill.

definition: To participate.
examples: Twenty teams took part in the game.
Everyone can take part.
She's taking part in a race.

definition: To answer rudely.
examples: Don't talk back to your mother.
He talked back to the teacher.
Kids who talk back get in trouble.

definition: To destroy a building.
examples: They tore down the old school.
The city is tearing down the bridge.
They want to tear down these houses.

definition: To tear into small pieces; to start to cry.
examples: She tore up his letter.
He teared up at the wedding.
Tear up the old receipts.

spanish.definition: Romper en pedazos; empezar a llorar.

definition: To have thoughts about someone or something; to consider.
examples: I'm thinking about you.
Think about it before you decide.
She thought about moving to Spain.

spanish.definition: Tener pensamientos sobre alguien o algo; considerar.

definition: To make a place neat.
examples: Tidy up your room before dinner.
We tidied up after the party.
She's tidying up the kitchen.

definition: To tie someone or something with rope.
examples: They tied up the boat.
The robbers tied up the guard.
Tie up the dog outside.

spanish.definition: Atar a alguien o algo con una cuerda.

definition: To test something; to compete for a place on a team.
examples: I want to try out the new app.
She tried out for the soccer team.
We're trying out a new recipe.

spanish.definition: Probar algo; competir por un lugar en un equipo.

definition: To become something different.
examples: The caterpillar turned into a butterfly.
Our trip turned into a disaster.
The rain is turning into snow.

definition: To use all of something.
examples: We used up all the milk.
Don't use up the hot water.
I've used up my vacation days.

spanish.definition: Usar todo lo que hay de algo.

definition: To stay until someone comes or something happens.
examples: Wait for me!
We waited for the bus for an hour.
I'm waiting for your answer.

spanish.definition: Quedarse hasta que alguien llegue o algo pase.

definition: To stay awake until someone comes home; to wait for someone.
examples: Don't wait up for me.
My mom waited up until I came home.
Hey, wait up!

spanish.definition: No dormirse hasta que alguien llegue; esperar a alguien.

definition: To leave suddenly because you are angry.
examples: He walked out of the meeting.
She walked out on her husband.
The workers walked out in protest.

spanish.definition: Irse de repente porque estás enojado.

definition: To use something until it is old; to make someone very tired.
examples: I wore out my shoes in a month.
Long walks wear out the dog.
These jeans are wearing out.

spanish.definition: Usar algo hasta dañarlo; cansar mucho a alguien.

definition: To relax after work.
examples: I watch TV to wind down.
She winds down with a hot bath.
The party wound down at midnight.

definition: To destroy completely.
examples: The flood wiped out the town.
The disease wiped out the birds.
The trip wiped out my savings.

definition: To spend time improving something.
examples: I need to work on my English.
She's working on a new book.
We worked on the project all night.

definition: To finish something; to put paper around something.
examples: Let's wrap up the meeting.
She wrapped up the gift.
We're wrapping up for the day.

spanish.definition: Acabar algo; poner papel alrededor de algo.

definition: Needing a lot of chewing.
examples: The steak is too chewy.
I like chewy cookies.
This candy is soft and chewy.

definition: Full of small bubbles.
examples: The kids love fizzy drinks.
This water is fizzy.
The soda isn't fizzy anymore.

definition: Full of lumps.
examples: This mattress is lumpy.
The sauce is lumpy.
She made lumpy mashed potatoes.

definition: Full of smoke; tasting of smoke.
examples: The room was very smoky.
I love the smoky taste of barbecue.
The air is smoky from the fires.

spanish.definition: Lleno de humo; con sabor a humo.

definition: Too wet and soft.
examples: The cereal got soggy.
My sandwich is soggy.
The ground is soggy after the rain.
